title: runbook lab benchmark notes - kvcache variance 2025-06-11
body:
Meeting: Runbook / Lab benchmark sync - KV-cache variance
Date: 2025-06-11
Attendees: Alex Chen (owner), Priya N., Diego M., Hannah L., Marcus F.
Duration: 50m
Location: #eng-bench Slack huddle + lab cluster

Agenda:
- Quick recap of Friday's regression signal
- Re-run targeted microbench harnesses across three model variants
- Validate KV-cache hit/miss patterns and batching behavior
- Decide next steps and temporary mitigation for production routes

Summary of issue:
Over the past 36 hours we observed a 12-18% tail-latency regression on p95 for the Llama-2-13B-quant endpoint when the autoscaler was in burst mode. Regression correlates with a higher-than-expected KV-cache miss rate and with frequent small batch sizes (~1-3) during traffic spikes. Not reproduced on stable non-quantized variants.

Environment / test harness used:
- Cluster: lab-gpu-3 (A100 40GB), CUDA 12.1, Triton-like runtime shim v0.9.2-feature-kvcache
- Model builds: llama-2-13b-q8a (build 2025-06-08), llama-2-13b-fp16 (control), rdw/smaller-13b-quant-test
- Test harness: bench-harness v2.7. Commands: 
  - ./bench-harness --cfg bench/kvcache-smoke.yaml --concurrency 8 --qps 80 --seed 42
  - ./bench-harness --trace-kvcache --out traces/jun11/
- Workload shape: mixture of short prompts (mean tokens 18) and medium (mean tokens 64), 80/20 split

Key runs and raw results (selected):
- Baseline (fp16 control): 10k requests, p50 42ms, p95 78ms, throughput 720 r/s
- Quant variant w/ current runtime (no patch): 10k requests, p50 48ms, p95 93ms, throughput 655 r/s, KV-cache hit-rate 76%
- Quant variant + deterministic-batcher toggle on: p50 45ms, p95 83ms, throughput 690 r/s, KV-cache hit-rate 81%
- Quant variant + kvcache-prefetch-experiment (lab flag): p50 44ms, p95 79ms, throughput 700 r/s, KV-cache hit-rate 86%
- Small-batch only test (simulate burst with many size=1 requests): p95 increased to 140ms on quant variant; kvcache-prefetch reduced p95 to 98ms but did not fully match fp16 control.

Observations:
- The largest delta is on p95 under small-batch conditions. p50 is relatively stable.
- KV-cache miss-rate correlates strongly with p95 increases. Misses are higher in quantized runs because of alignment/quant routines causing occasional cache population delays.
- Deterministic batcher helps by creating more consistent batch sizes, which reduces thrashing of the KV cache and improves kernel selection stability.
- Prefetching KV-cache entries shows the best immediate improvement in lab but requires careful memory sizing for larger models.
- No signs of GPU memory pressure (nvtop, nvidia-smi stable) during lab tests; CPU-side stalls observed in some worker threads during cache serialization.

Hypotheses / root-cause candidates:
1) Quantized model path introduces slight additional latency to initial KV cache population which, under small-batch bursty traffic, converts to more misses and higher tail latency.
2) Batcher heuristics are over-aggressive in preserving low latency for single-request flows and end up creating many tiny batches that increase KV population churn.
3) Some worker threads in runtime are yielding during serialization steps (lock contention) causing jitter.

Immediate mitigation options discussed:
- Enable deterministic-batcher for production routes serving quantized variants (config flag flip). Pros: quick; Cons: may change latency distribution for small single-request flows.
- Roll out kvcache-prefetch lab flag more widely in staging; measure memory impact.
- Add a lightweight delay/accumulator for single-request flows (20ms) to allow batch formation; A/B test with 5% traffic.
- Revert to non-quantized model for critical production route as emergency rollback (last resort).

Decisions made in meeting:
- Short-term: flip deterministic-batcher on for p-prod-q routes behind a feature flag and rollout to 10% traffic tomorrow 2025-06-12 AM (owner: Priya).
- Medium-term: run a 48-hour kvcache-prefetch canary on dedicated pool with increased memory limit (owner: Diego, starts 2025-06-12).
- Investigation: Marcus to add low-overhead KV-cache latency metrics and lock contention traces into bench-harness traces by 2025-06-13.
- Engineering spike: Hannah to prototype a minimal 20ms request accumulator in the batcher for single-request paths; target PR by 2025-06-18.

Action items (owner, due):
- Priya N.: deploy deterministic-batcher flag to 10% traffic, monitor p95 and error rates (due 2025-06-12)
- Diego M.: configure canary pool and run kvcache-prefetch 48h sweep; report memory usage and perf (due 2025-06-14)
- Marcus F.: instrument bench-harness for KV-cache latency histogram and thread lock waits; upload traces to traces/jun11/ (due 2025-06-13)
- Hannah L.: PR prototype for 20ms accumulator + microbench comparisons (due 2025-06-18)
- Alex C.: collate all run logs and prepare a short exec-friendly summary if rollback becomes necessary (due 2025-06-12)

Notes on experiments to reproduce at-home:
- Use bench/harness with --trace-kvcache and --dump-locks flags to capture worker-level events.
- Prefer steady-state runs at 25k requests with the exact same seed to compare hit-rate deltas.
- For small-batch emulation: --batch-size-target 1 --qps-spike-pattern "bursty:5s:20s"

Risks and monitoring signals:
- Risk: deterministic-batcher may slightly increase p50 for single-request latencies, which could impact interactive UX on some low-volume routes. Monitor p50 and p95 separately.
- Signal to watch: KV-cache miss-rate, kernel-selection churns per second, thread lock wait time, CPU syscall spikes.

Appendix - quick command snippets saved here:
- Run full trace: ./bench-harness --cfg bench/long-kvcache.yaml --trace-kvcache --dump-locks --out traces/jun11-full
- Compare two traces: python tools/trace-compare.py traces/jun11/quant-no-pf.json traces/jun11/quant-kvpf.json --metrics p95,kvcache-hit
- Toggle flag in staging: ./infra/deploy-toggle.sh deterministic_batcher true staging p-prod-q

Next sync: Friday 2025-06-13 10:30am. If short-term mitigation shows negative UX impact, emergency sync requested on 2025-06-12 5pm.

End of notes.
